newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thousands of Cambodians flee fighting to Thailand.
newsitem.headline: Thousands of Cambodians flee fighting to Thailand.

text.p: More than 20,000 Cambodian civilians fled into Thailand overnight to escape fighting in the besieged town of O'Smach, Thai military officials said on Tuesday.

Thai authorities decided to open the gates at a checkpoint and allowed the civilians to walk across the border late on Monday after fighting between royalist troops holding the town and troops under Cambodian strongman Hun Sen moved closer to the centre of the town.
"There was the sound of heavy gunfire in the evening and we learned that Hun Sen troops overran Khao Laem," a Thai army officer told Reuters.
Khao Laem, is a hill about five km (three miles) from O'Smach and was an important line of defence for the town's royalist defenders.
"Royalist troops are still in the town and the two sides are confronting each others just metres from each other," the Thai officer said.
Forces loyal to ousted Cambodian premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh have been fighting government troops under Hun Sen since shortly after the prince was ousted on July 6.
The refugees, most of them women and children, were allowed to seek temporary shelter at a border market about two km (one mile) inside Thailand.
Thai officials said the refugees would be transferred to a site some seven km (four miles) from the border which has been prepared for them, local Thai officials said.
